answer: One concrete defense is requiring every agent to prove control of a unique hardware-backed key before it can transact. A device's secure kernel signs a one-time attestation, binding the agent's identity to real silicon rather than to a free account anyone can duplicate. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of devices, not just a script. Like a falcon that can only hunt where it actually flies, each identity must prove real presence, and an ocean of cheap sock-puppets drains away because the cost of forging presence rises with every copy.
